record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.context_brief: Algebraic analysis of the Moisil-Theodoresco system
record.original_question: Apply the same algebraic analysis used for the Cauchy-Fueter system to the Moisil-Theodoresco system, the three-dimensional analogue and historical precursor of the Cauchy-Fueter system whose kernel has intrinsic physical interest and whose functions have natural regular extensions to H.

evidence.quote: Problem: Apply our algebraic analysis to the Moisil-Theodoresco system.
the so-called Moisil-Theodoresco system which is the 3-dimensional analogue ... of the Cauchy-Fueter system.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the real algebra of quaternions with basis $1,i,j,k$, and consider functions $f=f_0+if_1+jf_2+kf_3:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{H}$ of three real variables $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$. The Moisil–Theodoresco operator is the first-order linear differential operator
$$ M f \;=\; i\,\partial_{x_1} f + j\,\partial_{x_2} f + k\,\partial_{x_3} f, $$
and a function $f$ is called Moisil–Theodoresco regular when $Mf=0$. For several variables, consider $N$ copies $(x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(N)})\in(\mathbb{R}^3)^N$ with corresponding operators $M_1,\dots,M_N$, and let $\mathcal{R}$ denote the system $M_1 f = \dots = M_N f = 0$ acting on $\mathbb{H}$-valued functions of $3N$ real variables. Viewing $\mathcal{R}$ as a left module over the polynomial ring $R=\mathbb{R}[\xi^{(1)},\dots,\xi^{(N)}]$ obtained by symbol/Fourier transform (so $\partial_{x_\ell^{(m)}}\mapsto \xi_\ell^{(m)}$), perform the full algebraic analysis of this system. Specifically:

(i) Determine a minimal free resolution of the $R$-module $M_N := R^r / R^s A$ associated with the Moisil–Theodoresco system in $N$ variables, and identify the syzygies and compatibility conditions of the system.

(ii) Compute the Ext groups $\operatorname{Ext}^p_R(M_N,R)$ for all $p\geq 0$, and characterize the cohomological dimension and the projective dimension of $M_N$.

(iii) Use the resulting resolution to deduce the analytic properties of regular functions of several Moisil–Theodoresco variables: removability of compact singularities, Hartogs-type extension phenomena, the structure of the sheaf of solutions, and the dimensions of cohomology groups on suitable domains in $(\mathbb{R}^3)^N$.

(iv) Compare the results with those known for the Cauchy–Fueter system in several quaternionic variables, and describe explicitly the natural regular extensions of solutions to $\mathbb{H}^N$-valued Cauchy–Fueter regular functions.
artifact.status_search_result: Structural results for the Moisil–Theodoresco system in a single ℝ³ variable (resolution, structure theorem for solutions, right inverse, div-rot solvability) have been obtained, e.g., by Reyes (2008) and by Colombo–Luna-Elizarrarás–Sabadini–Shapiro–Struppa. Parts of the algebraic-analysis program (syzygies, Ext modules, cohomology) have been carried out in the one-variable case, but a complete several-variables treatment parallel to the Cauchy–Fueter system program does not appear to be fully published.

status_evidence.title: On the solutions of the Moisil–Théodoresco system
status_evidence.snippet: Structure theorem for the solutions of the Moisil–Théodoresco system in open subsets of ℝ³.
status_evidence.claim: One-variable structure theory of Moisil–Theodoresco solutions has been established.

status_evidence.title: A Quaternionic Treatment of the Inhomogeneous Div-rot System
status_evidence.snippet: Uses a right inverse of the Moisil–Teodorescu operator to give solvability conditions for the inhomogeneous div-rot system.
status_evidence.claim: Operator-theoretic/analytic tools developed for the one-variable Moisil–Theodoresco operator.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of Dirac Systems and Computational Algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph developing computational algebraic analysis for Dirac-type systems including Cauchy–Fueter in several variables.
status_evidence.claim: Algebraic-analysis machinery exists for Cauchy–Fueter; its application to several-variable Moisil–Theodoresco is not fully treated.
